title: Input hardening: lint hangs forever on a FIFO named *.md and reads /dev/zero unbounded (OOM)
description:
Reproduced: mkfifo /tmp/x.md && spk lint /tmp/x.md blocks forever (timed out, exit 124); /dev/zero hits the same unbounded read path and OOM-kills (confirmed mechanism, tested under ulimit). Ingestion uses std::fs::read_to_string with no file-type or size check (src/main.rs:486 and :1110).

RED: tests — (a) lint on a FIFO named *.md returns a labeled error within a timeout, never blocks; (b) lint on an oversized regular file (> cap) returns a labeled error naming the cap.
GREEN: require f.metadata()?.is_file() (or file_type().is_file()) before reading; enforce a size cap (e.g. 2 MiB — corpus files are ~10-50 KB) with a remediation hint naming the offending path. Same treatment for compile/verify/graph ingestion paths that share the discovery code.
Evidence: review round 2, issue 6.
notes: SCOPE ADDITION 2026-09-29 (review round 2, path-to-prod step 4): include codegen identifier sanitizing hardening in this ticket — verify compile's row-id → Rust-identifier sanitization (src/compile.rs law-case fn naming) covers hostile ids (leading digits, unicode, reserved words, extremely long ids) with a RED test per class; the ingestion file-type check and the codegen sanitizer share the 'hostile input' theme and both gate trust in emitted artifacts.

title: Explore: contract-wiring checker — spec-level interface impedance from declared dataflow
description:
Exploration ticket (Rule-of-5 reviewed design conversation, 2026-09-29). Goal: decide whether a checker can detect interface absence and impedance at the SPEC level, using only declared/typed wiring — no source analysis.

Detectable structural patterns (from spk graph edges):
1. Published-unconsumed: extension_point Constraint with zero inbound satisfies edges.
2. Consumed-unpublished: satisfies pointing at nonexistent/unpublished contract (dangling or typing violation today — check if the message is interface-shaped enough).
3. Emitted-unobserved: emits→effect with zero observes (cross-ref add-observability-contracts change; avoid duplicating its linter.observability).
4. Unlinked expectation: a consumer-side constraint describing a contract's shape with NO derives_from edge to the producer's published contract constraint — the spec-level analog of an untyped interface. Weakest but most novel signal.

Hard precondition: all patterns require corpora to declare wiring in structured cells; prose wiring is invisible (evidence: bajan's extraction.claims→eval.claims wiring lives in prose only — CORR-001). Impedance proper (shape divergence) is only comparable where BOTH sides model contract shape as structured rows.

Exploration deliverable: spike notes answering (a) which patterns are worth a linter spec, (b) false-positive rate against this repo's corpus + bajan, (c) whether severity should be advisory. Output feeds a real change proposal (spec + linter spec file) — NOT implementation in this ticket.

Per repo TDD discipline: define test shapes before any checker spec — for each pattern, the fixture corpus, expected finding, and severity.
acceptance_criteria: Spike notes exist answering (a)(b)(c); each candidate pattern has a defined fixture/test shape or is rejected with evidence; decision recorded whether to proceed to a change proposal; no production code changes in this ticket
notes: REVIEW FIXES (issue-review, converged pass 5): (1) Spike-notes destination: commit as openspec/research/contract-wiring-spike.md (house precedent: specodelic-4ae decision note under openspec/). (2) Meter (run verbatim at base_commit): cargo run -q -- graph -j specs | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(len(d['data']['graph']['violations']))" — expect 38; per-pattern fixture corpora live in tests/cli.rs fixtures once a proposal lands. title: [bug/gh#4] explain dual-format overpromises: section-sync not enforced by spk lint; footer hint cites nonexistent Notes field
description:
From gh issue charly-vibes/specodelic#4 (adopter, spk 0.1.0; verified on main 2026-09-29).

1. {"ok":true,"envelope_version":"0.1","cli_version":"0.1.0","envelope_kind":"ok","data":{"body":"# dual-format

Where specodelic meets **OpenSpec**: this repo manages its engineering
change workflow in openspec (proposals → tasks → archive), and every
change delta is also a lint-clean specodelic file. One markdown file,
two parsers, requirement text authored once.

A **dual-format file** carries both grammars:

- Specodelic half: YAML frontmatter (`id: spec`, `kind: intent`, an
  EARS `statement`) plus the `## Constraints`, `## Model`, and
  `## Properties` tables.
- Openspec half: `## Purpose`, `## ADDED Requirements`, and a sibling
  `## Requirements` section with identical text.

**Naming law**: openspec hard-requires the delta filename `spec.md`,
so dual-format files declare `id: spec` (the `-` ⇔ `.` mapping makes
that the legal id). Uniqueness is per-file — any number of `id: spec`
files coexist. Deltas stay self-contained: `[[wiki-refs]]` resolve
only within the file; domain semantics are cited by prose path
(`specs/<name>.md`), never wiki-link.

**Enforcement**: `linter.dual_format_valid` — a file carrying
`## ADDED Requirements` must declare `id: spec` and pair it with the
sibling `## Requirements` section; a capability spec under
`openspec/specs/` must be dual-format or CI fails. The section-sync
check fails on drift between the two requirement sections.

**Migration** (plain openspec file → compliant):

1. Add the frontmatter: `id: spec`, `kind: intent`, one EARS `SHALL`
   statement condensing the requirements.
2. Derive the tables: one `invariant` Constraint per MUST the
   requirements imply, a Model covering the scenarios, one unit
   Property deriving from each constraint (the coverage rule).
3. Mirror `## Requirements` (identical text to `## ADDED
   Requirements`); a plain capability spec keeps only
   `## Requirements`.
4. Gates: `spk lint <file>`, `openspec validate --all --strict`, and
   the section-sync check must all pass.","format_revision":"specodelic.md Revision 8","topic":"dual-format"},"warnings":[],"hints":[{"command":"→ Run: apply the format, then check with: specodelic lint","description":"apply the format, then check with: specodelic lint

Drifted-mirror fixture lints clean (verified). FIX (this ticket): implement requirement-section drift detection in the linter — a file carrying both ## ADDED Requirements and ## Requirements must have identical section text; new finding in the dual_format_valid family (extend the rule or add requirement_drift), RULE_TABLE entry, tests, spec/docs sync.
2. lint failure footer hint (src/main.rs:913) says 'cite the governing constraint in Notes if it's a false positive' — no Notes field exists anywhere in the format. Reword to point at what exists (spk explain lint-rules).

title: [feature/gh#2.1] bare row refs in id:spec dual-format files: resolve against own rows (or document the file-qualification requirement with an example)
description:
From gh issue charly-vibes/specodelic#2 point 1. RE-SCOPED after issue-review 2026-09-29: the 'document the file-qualification requirement' leg is DONE (specodelic-ar2/gh#3 + specodelic-vi2: explain references/dual-format + scaffold + self-file hint). REMAINING SCOPE — the enforcement decision only:

Option A: bare row refs in id:spec files resolve against their OWN rows (compat: bare [[c]] currently is metasyntactic-skipped by is_metasyntactic — dotless unknown targets vanish silently; lint.rs total_refs + graph.rs resolve() must both change, plus the coverage rule's bare-id arm derived.contains(*cid) already accepts the bare form).
Option B: keep file-qualification mandatory but make the metasyntactic skip stop eating dotted-less row refs silently (emit a labeled finding instead of silence).

MUST: an id:spec fixture with [[row-id]] behaves per the chosen option in BOTH lint and graph; decision recorded as a comment on this ticket before implementation (HITL: affects every existing dual-format author). Corpus behavior must not change for file-qualified refs.
METER: cargo test; spk lint + graph on a synthetic dual-format fixture pair.
ANTI-GOALS: no change to cross-file resolution for non-dual ids; no new spec revision required if Option B.
FILES: src/lint.rs, src/graph.rs. File-header required.

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: Empirical finding from the specodelic-ar2 Ro5 review (2026-09-29): the file-qualification law documented for gh#3 is NOT what the checkers enforce. Fixture: id:spec file with guard [[c]] and derives_from [[c]] (bare, dotless) — spk lint = 0 issues (metasyntactic skip), coverage's bare-id arm (lint.rs derived.contains(*cid)) COUNTS it as covering, spk graph = 0 dangling but 0 edges (silent vanish). Bare TEXT (no brackets) is the only loudly-failing form (no_orphan_property). So the 'document the file-qualification requirement' leg of this ticket is done (guide/gh#3), but the checker-side work remains: either enforce the law (reject bare row refs in id:spec files / make bare refs resolve against own rows = this ticket's original ask) or align coverage's bare-id acceptance with the documented law. Also relevant: is_metasyntactic's dotless skip is what eats the refs — any enforcement change must decide what happens to the scaffold's old '[[id]]' pattern consumers may have copied.

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: Decision of record (user-approved 2026-09-29): Option A — bare row refs in id:spec files resolve against the file's OWN rows, in both lint and graph. Rationale: the self-containment law (#42) already scopes id:spec resolution file-locally, so a dotless target naming an own row has exactly one possible meaning; and the coverage rule already accepted the bare form, so Option B would have left two rules contradicting each other. Scope: dotless targets only (dotful keep the gh#5 hint — genuinely ambiguous with file.row); unknown bare targets keep the metasyntactic skip; typing violations on bare refs become visible. Implemented TDD: 4 tests; corpus churn zero.

title: [feature/gh#2.2] corpus discovery: bare spk lint finds nothing in consumer repos — configured corpus path or a discovery hint
description:
From gh issue charly-vibes/specodelic#2 point 2. In a consumer repo (openspec-managed, dual-format corpus under openspec/changes/*/specs/), bare spk lint reports 'no spec files found' even with 14 dual-format files present; spk doctor passes all checks and does not hint at it; the working invocation spk lint openspec had to be found by trial.

Options (pick at design time): (a) honor a configured corpus path — env var (e.g. SPECODELIC_CORPUS) and/or a line in the SPECODELIC managed block that spk init writes, so bare spk lint works after init; (b) minimal: when lint/graph find zero files and an openspec/ tree exists, the failure hint should say 'found an openspec/ tree — try: spk lint openspec'; (c) doctor gains a corpus-discovery check that names the discovery rule ('pass a directory containing *.md specs; hidden and build dirs are skipped').

Drive the six Checker Ownership checkers in dependency order (skip dependents on failure, run independent branches regardless), then coverage, compile, model_check, verify in sequence — gating each stage transition on the exact guards specs/specodelic.md specifies, never looser or stricter. external_completeness runs when a checklist exists but never gates. rename stays out of scope.

MUST: a corpus run reports each stage's outcome; the first failing stage halts its dependents (skipped, not failed) while independent branches still report; stage sequence matches specodelic.md's lifecycle (draft → parsed → linted → compiled → model_checked → verified).
METER: `spk orchestrate specs --json` → .data lists every stage with status; halt/skip behavior proven by a synthetic fixture with one failing checker.
ANTI-GOALS: no looser/stricter gating than specified; no rename triggering; no silent skips (every skip is reported).
REGRESSION: cargo test — existing suites keep passing.
FILES: src/orchestrate.rs + main.rs Orchestrate subcommand (file-header required; shared main.rs with sibling pipeline tickets).

Depends on specodelic-1pv (last pipeline stage) and specodelic-b15 (all six Checker Ownership checkers must exist first). HITL: whether the orchestrator also owns draft→parsed — see specodelic-mp1 before closing.

title: Implement specodelic rename: atomic id rename with link rewrite

METER: rename integration test on a tempdir fixture (definition + cross-file links) + the graph check above.
ANTI-GOALS: no partial renames (atomicity is the point); batch/whole-namespace rename out of scope pending HITL (rename.md Needs Human Review — see specodelic-mp1).

FILES: src/rename.rs; reuse graph.rs (do not re-derive). File-header required.

Builds on the existing graph command (done).

title: Implement specodelic verify: execute proptest blocks + gate
description:
Per specs/verify.md. Run every proptest! block compile produced to completion; transition a file to verified only when all pass AND model_check's most recent run against the CURRENT compiled artifact is clean.

MUST: a file with a failing proptest block is NOT verified; a file whose model_check result is stale (artifact changed since the run) is NOT verified; only the conjunction verifies.
METER: `spk verify <file> --json` → .data.status == "verified" exactly in that case, else the blocking stage is named.
ANTI-GOALS: never bypass the model_check guard; never cache/assume artifacts are current; never treat a skipped stage as passed.
REGRESSION: cargo test — existing suites keep passing.
FILES: src/verify.rs + main.rs Verify subcommand (file-header required; shared main.rs with sibling pipeline tickets).

Depends on specodelic-lnq (proptest blocks) and specodelic-nx7 (clean-run guard).

title: Implement specodelic model-check: TLC/Alloy against compiled module
description:
Per specs/model_check.md. Run the model checker against compile's output; report no_counterexample-within-bound or counterexample (TLC path). Distinguish model_checked (a run happened) from no_counterexample (no violation) — CLAR-003.

IMPLEMENTED (add-model-check, Decision 3 Option A approved): spk model-check <files> [--max-depth 100] [--max-states] [--timeout-secs] — native stateright backend interprets the compiled ModelIR as a pc-automaton (init = first listed state, transitions as always-enabled actions, matching the committed .tla semantics); explores exhaustively within the bound; reached cap => timed_out (never collapsed into clean); missing compiled artifact => labeled missing_artifact error with a spk compile hint; run reports persist as <stem>.check.json carrying the consumed .tla's SHA-256 for verify's staleness check (rerun_on_model_change).

AMENDED MUST per approval: the corpus language has no executable predicate semantics, so the native backend checks no user invariants and reports invariants_checked: [] honestly; the counterexample leg (synthetic spec with violated invariant yields trace naming the invariant) is DEFERRED to the predicate-fragment decision — new HITL row on specodelic-mp1; TLC backend moved to specodelic-ug3.
